reports.title: Big Oil’s Windfall Quarter: Exxon and Chevron at Record Highs
reports.summary: Exxon earned $15.4 billion and set $20 billion of 2027 buybacks; Chevron’s profit nearly tripled. Where the money came from, what they do with it and what it says about the oil market.

reports.title: Inflation Is Back: The Fed, the ECB and the BoJ at a Crossroads
reports.summary: US PCE inflation at 3.6%, a split Fed, an ECB losing Lagarde early and a Bank of Japan at its 2% target. Where each central bank stands, what markets price and what to watch into December.

reports.title: Tech’s Worst Day Since June: Intel, Chips and the AI Payoff Question
reports.summary: Intel fell 29% on a weak guide, the chip index lost 7.2% and the Nasdaq 2.9%. What moved, why it spread across the chain and what it says about where the AI cycle stands.

reports.title: The Truce That Isn’t on Paper: US-China After 10 November
reports.summary: The US-China truce is extended in politics to 10 January, but its legal texts still expire on 9 and 10 November. What lapses, how tariffs and trade have shifted, and what is at stake for markets.

reports.title: The $730 Billion Question: Big Tech’s AI Capex and What It Means for Investors
reports.summary: Cloud growth accelerated at Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon, yet the market sold two of them as capex outran cash flow. The results, the funding, the accounting and the scenarios for 2027.

reports.title: The Binance Breach
reports.summary: Billions left Binance hot wallets, issuers froze about $1.8 billion of stablecoins and Bitcoin fell below $79,000. What is confirmed, what is only claimed, and what it means for a market in a bear phase.

reports.title: Midterms 2026: What Markets Are Pricing
reports.summary: Prediction markets and models point to a change in control of at least one chamber on 3 November. What is priced, the Senate races that decide it, what history says and what each outcome means for policy.

reports.title: The US Consumer at the Limit
reports.summary: Sentiment near record lows, gasoline above $4 and real wages falling, yet retailers forecast a first trillion-dollar holiday season. What holds spending up, who carries it and where it could crack.

reports.title: Europe’s Winter Gas Squeeze
reports.summary: TTF crossed €100/MWh for the first time since 2022 with storage at a record low for the season. Prices, storage, the contest with Asia for LNG, policy, exposed industries and the winter outlook.

reports.title: Big Tech’s AI Bill Comes Due
reports.summary: Alphabet, Microsoft and Meta all grew revenue by about a fifth or more in the September quarter, but the market only paid where operating cash covered the spending. The three quarters compared.

reports.title: What Happened to You, France? Public Finances, Bond Markets and Politics in 2026
reports.summary: Record debt, a deficit twice the euro-area average and three governments lost since 2024. France now borrows above Italy. The fiscal trajectory, the bond market, ratings and the politics behind them.

reports.title: Anthropic: Growth, Capital and the Road to a Public Listing
reports.summary: Annualised revenue has risen from about $1bn to more than $65bn in nineteen months and the company is preparing to list. What the latest data show and what an IPO valuation would assume.

reports.title: Capital Expenditure, Depreciation and the Quality of US Earnings
reports.summary: AI chips are expensed over five or six years while the chipmaker books the profit at once. How much that timing gap and other AI-era accounting flatter S&P 500 earnings, and when the bill arrives.

reports.title: Financing the AI Build-Out in 2027: The $1.2 Trillion Question
reports.summary: AI infrastructure spending passes $1 trillion next year, more than Big Tech’s own cash covers. Who funds the gap, through which markets, at what cost, and where the risk ends up.

reports.title: EUR/USD: An In-Depth Assessment
reports.summary: The euro is at its lowest against the dollar since May 2025 after four weekly declines. The drivers, from monetary policy and energy to French fiscal stress, tested against the data.

reports.title: USD/CNY: A Quantitative Review
reports.summary: The renminbi is at its strongest against the dollar since mid-2022, in a move tightly managed by the People’s Bank of China. How controlled the trend is and how the central bank is now slowing it.

reports.title: USD/CAD: A Quantitative Review
reports.summary: The dollar is at a one-year high against the Canadian dollar in one of the calmest moves on record. Why oil has stopped helping the loonie, and what the numbers say before the Bank of Canada meets.

reports.title: AUD/USD: A Quantitative Review
reports.summary: The Australian dollar is still up for the year, helped by the most hawkish central bank in the G10, but it has lost almost 4% in a month. The trend break, record-low volatility and the role of risk appetite.

reports.title: USD/CHF: A Quantitative Review
reports.summary: The dollar has gained more than 5% against the Swiss franc this year, making the franc one of the weakest major currencies. How stretched the move is and what could reverse it.

reports.title: GBP/USD: A Quantitative Review
reports.summary: Sterling has slipped to a three-month low while gilt yields hit their highest since 2007. How the pound trades, what drives it and what the numbers imply before the 28 October Budget.

reports.title: USD/JPY: A Quantitative Review
reports.summary: Dollar-yen is back near 158, close to where Tokyo and Washington intervened in July. The trend, volatility, tail risk and drivers of the pair, and what the numbers say about the coming weeks.

reports.title: ASML
reports.summary: Every advanced chip is printed on an ASML machine. Sales guidance is up about 16% and next year’s EUV capacity is almost sold out, but China and the pace of AI spending make the shares volatile.

reports.title: AMD
reports.summary: Data centre revenue doubled, rack-scale AI systems are shipping and three of the largest AI developers have signed up. The shares have roughly tripled and trade above the average target.

reports.title: Broadcom
reports.summary: The designer of custom AI chips for the largest AI developers says its AI revenue will double next year and again the year after. The shares are still a quarter below their high on fears of competition.

reports.title: JPMorgan Chase: Earnings Preview
reports.summary: The largest US bank reports on 13 October after a record second quarter. Management has guided to strong trading and dealmaking again, but its own executives say the cycle feels almost too good.

reports.title: Amazon
reports.summary: AWS is growing at its fastest pace in four years and earns most of the profit, but AI data centre spending has turned free cash flow negative. Whether the bet pays back.

reports.title: Constellation Brands
reports.summary: Second-quarter results beat expectations, but the beat came from refilling distributor warehouses rather than from more people buying Modelo and Corona. What the numbers say about demand.

reports.title: FOMC Minutes: September Meeting
reports.summary: The Fed raised rates unanimously in September, but the minutes show a committee that agreed on the move far more than on the reasons. Most officials expect one more increase by year end.

reports.title: Alphabet
reports.summary: Search still grows, Google Cloud is up 82% and the antitrust cases ended without a break-up. The price is $200 billion of capex a year and the first negative cash flow quarter in two decades.

reports.title: Coca-Cola
reports.summary: One of its best years in a decade, under a new chief executive and with volumes growing again. The business model, the shift from price to volume, the $20 billion tax dispute and the valuation.
